timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hi, I'm Oglaia, for Wai. I'm a Surina Mies and I'm studying hydrology and water resources here at IHG.
I'm a second year master student. Studying at IHG Delft was pretty much a whole new experience for me.
It's totally different than studying back home and a highlight for me was actually
when I successfully finished the first part of this study and passed to start my research.

I started to do my research study now and my research I'm conducting in Uganda and I'm doing a assessment of the impacts of urbanization and climate change on the ground water balance of campala in Uganda.
We went on a field trip as a part of our research program and it was actually a nice experience.
We went to Italy and southern France. It was very nice in terms of learning two different languages, especially in doing our field work.
We had to conferred with people and these people were only talking French basically.
That was a really nice experience and I enjoyed it.
If I could give somebody advice to do a master's study at IHG Delft, I would say it is a really good opportunity to do it
because especially if it's somebody from outside the Netherlands because it's a total different community also at IHG.
It's like the world at a small space and I would highly recommend doing a master's study at IHG.

Studying in Delft is like I experienced the city from another side, different than being a tourist in the Netherlands and what I think about Delft, if I compare it to other cities of the Netherlands, it's really a student city.
But I still like it in terms of if I go to Amsterdam or Rotterdam, those places are more crowded.

At IHG there's like a multi-cultural aspect because of the fact that the people from all around the world, and it's a really good opportunity to learn from all the other cultures because you experience the differences of the other cultures.

But also I found some similarities between let me say my culture and how we do some things and in our part of the world, like in Suriname, in South America, in the Caribbean and like other parts of the world.
So that was like one of the things I really appreciated about this multi-cultural environment at IHG.
I also had the opportunity to participate in a couple of social events at IHG.
For instance, the sports day, there was a famous one. I joined the Women Football Team where we had I think the third place and I also joined the running team of the IHG.
We were champion there, that was really nice.
And another nice thing is the social nights where you have different parts of the world performing their culture.
And for us, it was also really nice because I think it was the first time that there was a big Caribbean community performing.
So we did a very hard and it was a really nice evening.
So the social events are like another part of IHG where you come together as students to learn from each other.

youtube_channel: IHE Delft Institute for Water Education
youtube_description:
Oclaya Sophia Verwey is from Suriname, South America. Her background is in geology. When Oclaya graduated from the University she wanted to pursue a career in groundwater. When she googled Master of Science in water resources, IHE Delft popped up and so she started following IHE Delft. Last year, she came to IHE Delft for a short course financed by her employer. In that period the SIDS scholarship started, and so Oclaya applied for the year 2017. She had a choice between the Erasmus Mundus and SIDS scholarship, but she decided to apply for the SIDS scholarship.

Why she choose IHE Delft over other Institutes: ‘’At IHE Delft everything is combined in one programme: the scientific and engineering part. It matched my expectations.’’

Read her testimonial here https://www.un-ihe.org/oclaya-sophia-verwey-testimonial
youtube_title: IHE Delft 💧 Interview with MSc student Oclaya Sophia Verwey
